title: Ex 2.5 #10 · Make ((P ∧ Q) ∨ R) ⇒ (R ∨ S) false
prompt: The statement $((P \wedge Q) \vee R) \Rightarrow (R \vee S)$ is false. Find the truth values of $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$. You can reason this out without a full truth table.
answer_format: Truth values for P, Q, R and S, like P = T, Q = F, R = T, S = F.
answer: P = T, Q = T, R = F, S = F
hints: An implication is false in only one situation: its hypothesis is true and its conclusion is false.
Start with the conclusion R ∨ S being false. What does that say about R and S? Then use the hypothesis.
solution: For the implication to be false, $(P \wedge Q) \vee R$ must be true and $R \vee S$ must be false.
$R \vee S$ is false only when $R$ and $S$ are both false.
With $R$ false, $(P \wedge Q) \vee R$ can only be true if $P \wedge Q$ is true, so $P$ and $Q$ are both true.
So P = T, Q = T, R = F, S = F.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the truth tables for ∧, ∨, ∼, ⇒ and ⇔ (Sections 2.2–2.5).
